## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Objective
- The user said only “Minecraft”; the assistant interpreted this as building a polished browser-based Minecraft-style voxel sandbox.

- Built an original “BLOCKCRAFT” voxel game rather than using Minecraft assets/trademarks.

210:       particles.splice(i, 1)
211:       continue
212:     }
213:     p.vel.y -= 20 * dt
214:     p.mesh.position.addScaledVector(p.vel, dt)
215:     p.mesh.rotation.x += p.spin.x * dt
216:     p.mesh.rotation.y += p.spin.y * dt
217:     p.mesh.material.opacity = Math.min(1, p.life / 0.35)
218:     p.mesh.scale.multiplyScalar(1 - dt * 0.45)

224: const heldScene = new THREE.Scene()
225: const heldCamera = new THREE.OrthographicCamera(-1, 1, 1, -1, 0.1, 10)
226: heldCamera.position.set(0, 0, 4)
227: heldCamera.lookAt(0, 0, 0)
228: const heldAmbient = new THREE.AmbientLight(0xffffff, 1.8)
229: const heldLight = new THREE.DirectionalLight(0xffffff, 2.1)
230: heldLight.position.set(2, 3, 4)

235:   map: getAtlasTexture(),
236:   transparent: true,
237:   alphaTest: 0.08,
238:   side: THREE.DoubleSide,

242: function tileUv(tile, corners) {
243:   const col = tile % 8
244:   const row = (tile / 8) | 0
245:   return corners.map(([u, v]) => [(col + u) / 8, (7 - row + v) / 8])
246: }
247: 
248: const BOX_UV_ORDER = [
249:   [0, 1],
250:   [1, 1],
251:   [0, 0],
252:   [1, 0],
253: ]

255: function setHeldBlock(id) {
256:   const def = BLOCKS[id]
257:   if (!def) return
258:   let geo
259:   if (def.cross) {
260:     geo = new THREE.PlaneGeometry(0.95, 0.95)
261:     const uvs = tileUv(def.tex[0], BOX_UV_ORDER)
262:     geo.attributes.uv.array.set(uvs.flat())
263:     geo.attributes.uv.needsUpdate = true
264:   } else {
265:     geo = new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.9, 0.9, 0.9)
266:     const uvArray = geo.attributes.uv.array
267:     for (let f = 0; f < 6; f++) {
268:       const uvs = tileUv(def.tex[f], BOX_UV_ORDER)
269:       for (let v = 0; v < 4; v++) {
270:         const i = (f * 4 + v) * 2
271:         uvArray[i] = uvs[v][0]
272:         uvArray[i + 1] = uvs[v][1]
273:       }
274:     }
275:     geo.attributes.uv.needsUpdate = true
276:   }
277:   if (heldMesh) {
278:     heldPivot.remove(heldMesh)
279:     heldMesh.geometry.dispose()
280:   }
281:   heldMesh = new THREE.Mesh(geo, heldMaterial)
282:   heldPivot.add(heldMesh)
283:   heldPivot.rotation.set(0.18, -0.65, 0.08)
284: }

738: function moveJoystick(clientX, clientY) {

742:   const dist = Math.hypot(dx, dy)
743:   if (dist > radius) {
744:     dx = (dx / dist) * radius
745:     dy = (dy / dist) * radius
746:   }
747:   touchMove.x = dx / radius
748:   touchMove.y = -dy / radius
749:   stick.style.transform = `translate(${dx}px, ${dy}px)`

function drawTileTo(ctx, tile, dx, dy, dw, dh) {
  const { canvas } = getAtlas()
  const ox = (tile % ATLAS_COLS) * TILE
  const oy = Math.floor(tile / ATLAS_COLS) * TILE
  ctx.imageSmoothingEnabled = false
  ctx.drawImage(canvas, ox, oy, TILE, TILE, dx, dy, dw, dh)
}

function drawFace(ctx, tile, p0, p1, p2, p3, shadeAlpha = 0) {
  const ux = (p1[0] - p0[0]) / TILE
  const uy = (p1[1] - p0[1]) / TILE
  const vx = (p3[0] - p0[0]) / TILE
  const vy = (p3[1] - p0[1]) / TILE
  ctx.save()
  ctx.setTransform(ux, uy, vx, vy, p0[0], p0[1])
  drawTileTo(ctx, tile, 0, 0, TILE, TILE)
  ctx.restore()
  if (shadeAlpha > 0) {
    ctx.save()
    ctx.setTransform(ux, uy, vx, vy, p0[0], p0[1])
    ctx.fillStyle = `rgba(0,0,0,${shadeAlpha})`
    ctx.fillRect(0, 0, TILE, TILE)
    ctx.restore()
  }
}

export function blockIcon(id, size = 64) {
  const def = BLOCKS[id]
  const canvas = document.createElement('canvas')
  canvas.width = size
  canvas.height = size
  const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d')
  ctx.imageSmoothingEnabled = false
  if (!def) return canvas
  if (def.cross) {
    drawTileTo(ctx, def.tex[0], size * 0.1, size * 0.05, size * 0.8, size * 0.9)
    return canvas
  }
  const s = size
  const top = [s * 0.5, s * 0.07]
  const right = [s * 0.93, s * 0.3]
  const bottom = [s * 0.5, s * 0.53]
  const left = [s * 0.07, s * 0.3]
  const dl = [s * 0.07, s * 0.73]
  const dr = [s * 0.5, s * 0.96]
  const rr = [s * 0.93, s * 0.73]

  drawFace(ctx, def.tex[2], left, top, right, bottom, 0)
  drawFace(ctx, def.tex[0], left, dl, dr, bottom, 0.22)
  drawFace(ctx, def.tex[4], bottom, dr, rr, right, 0.08)
  return canvas
}

# BLOCKCRAFT

A handcrafted voxel sandbox that runs in the browser. Explore an infinite procedural world, mine and place blocks, build a base, watch the sun go down, and meet the local wildlife.

Built with [Three.js](https://threejs.org/) and [Vite](https://vite.dev/).

## Play

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open the URL Vite prints (the project defaults to port `3002`). To make a production build:

```bash
npm run build
npm run preview
```

## Controls

| Input | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `W` `A` `S` `D` | Move |
| Mouse | Look (click the world to capture the cursor) |
| Left mouse | Mine / hold to break |
| Right mouse | Place selected block |
| `Space` | Jump (ascend while flying) |
| `Shift` | Sprint |
| `Ctrl` | Crouch (descend while flying) |
| `1`–`9` / wheel | Choose hotbar slot |
| `E` | Open the block palette |
| `F` | Toggle flying |
| `F3` | Debug overlay |
| `Esc` | Pause / release the cursor |

On phones and tablets, drag the left thumbstick to move, drag the right side of the screen to look, and use the buttons for jump, mine, place, fly, and the block palette. The layout respects notches and other safe-area insets.

## Features

- Infinite chunked terrain with plains, forests, deserts, snowy peaks, beaches, caves, ore veins, lakes, trees, flowers, cacti, and pumpkins.
- Per-face ambient occlusion baked into chunk meshes, with distance fog and a full day/night cycle.
- Mining with block-specific hardness, placement, block particles, a held-item view, and synthesized Web Audio effects.
- Pigs, sheep, and chickens wandering the landscape.
- Creative block palette with 26 block types, isometric inventory icons, and a nine-slot hotbar.
- Procedural texture atlas generated at runtime — no external art assets.
- Worlds are saved to `localStorage`; edits, time of day, and the spawn point survive reloads.
- Shareable world seeds through the URL (`?seed=...`).

## Project layout

```text
src/
  main.js      game loop, input, HUD, saving, held item, particles
  world.js     terrain generation, chunk meshing, AO, trees, spawn clearing
  player.js    movement, collision, camera, block raycasting
  blocks.js    texture atlas, block registry, inventory icons
  mobs.js      low-poly animals
  sky.js       sky shader, sun/moon, stars, clouds, lighting
  audio.js     procedural sound effects
  noise.js     deterministic noise and hashing helpers
  style.css    menu, HUD, touch controls, responsive layouts
```

## Development notes

The renderer uses `MeshLambertMaterial` and baked vertex colours rather than real-time shadows, keeping the scene light enough for laptops and phones. World edits are stored as a compact list of chunk-local indices. Software-rendered browsers (such as Playwright's SwiftShader fallback) will report much lower frame rates than a real GPU.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a polished browser-based Minecraft-style voxel sandbox from the single user prompt “Minecraft,” with procedural terrain, mining, building, exploration, day/night, mobs, and desktop/mobile controls.

## Requirements
- No explicit requirements beyond “Minecraft.”
- Must build and serve as a static site from this repository.
- Mobile touch support is expected, including safe areas and usable touch controls.
- Visual verification should use Playwright; software rendering must be reported as SwiftShader/CPU rather than hardware GPU.

## Decisions
- Built an original game called “BLOCKCRAFT” rather than using Minecraft assets or trademarks.
- Used Vite + Three.js (`three` 0.180.0, `vite` 7.3.7) with a procedural canvas texture atlas.
- Terrain is chunked at 16×16×64 with biomes, trees, flowers, cacti, pumpkins, ores, water, and caves.
- Baked ambient occlusion and per-face shading into vertex colors; avoided real-time shadows for performance.
- Added creative hotbar/inventory, block mining/placing, held-block view, particles, synthesized audio, mobs, sky/day-night, clouds, stars, and `localStorage` saves.
- Menu uses a cinematic low orbit around spawn with terrain clearance; mobile gets a compact landscape header.
- Touch layout uses a scaled hotbar, hides the held block, and displays touch-specific instructions.

## Work State
### Completed
- Full game implementation and UI: `index.html`, `src/style.css`, `src/main.js`, `src/world.js`, `src/player.js`, `src/sky.js`, `src/audio.js`, `src/mobs.js`, `src/blocks.js`, `src/noise.js`.
- Fixed dark/black side-face artifacts with raised face shades and AO floor.
- Improved menu camera to show sky and horizon; fixed logo overflow on phones; fixed compact landscape logo.
- Fixed mobile hotbar overflow, pause-button interception by `#lookZone`, overlapping fly/inventory buttons, toast clipping, and held-block clutter.
- Added touch-specific pause and inventory hints.
- Fixed spawn consistency: saves now include `spawn`; spawn clearing is recorded as edits and only applied to new worlds.
- Verified desktop gameplay, mining, placing, inventory, pause/resume, day/night, water shoreline, save/reload, mobile touch controls, and responsive layouts.
- Verified production build (`npm run build`) and production preview on port 3003.
- Updated `README.md` with gameplay, controls, features, layout, and development notes.
- Added `dist/` to `.gitignore`.

### Active
- Final verification and cleanup only.

### Blocked
- Playwright uses SwiftShader software rendering; measured FPS is roughly 2–8, so real GPU performance cannot be judged here.

## Next Move
1. Re-run `npm run build` after the latest UI/text changes.
2. Optionally re-check production preview and take final desktop/mobile screenshots.
3. Review final `git status` and ensure no unintended generated files are tracked.
4. Report completion, noting SwiftShader software rendering for FPS observations.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: game loop, input, UI orchestration, saving, spawn, held item, particles.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js`: terrain generation, meshing, AO, trees, spawn clearing, save data.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/style.css`: menu, HUD, touch controls, responsive and mobile rules.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: page structure and UI markup.
